physics_configuration.device: Square array of cylindrical pillars (epsilon 4.0, silicon nitride at 1.55 um) on a 1.0 um period, 0.6 um tall, in air with no substrate. The radius of each pillar is the hyperbolic lens phase of a 150 um focal length at 1.55 um wrapped onto 0.15 to 0.42 um; the array is lens-like and its focusing efficiency is not claimed. The geometry is rasterized on cell centres into the epsilon tensor (no project structures).
physics_configuration.source: soft Ex plane sheet at z = -0.8 um spanning the lateral CPML (extend_through_pml), Gaussian pulse of 15 fs power FWHM centred at 30 fs, carrier 1.55 um; the source envelope ends at 84.7 fs
physics_configuration.monitor: z-normal FieldMonitor at z = +0.6 um (0.4 um above the pillar tops) spanning the footprint, downsample 8 (0.4 um samples, sin(theta_max) = 1.55/0.8 covers every propagating angle), six components, DFT at 1.65, 1.55 and 1.45 um
physics_configuration.objective: sum over the three wavelengths of |E|^2 on the axis 150 um beyond the monitor plane, evaluated by torchfdtd.angular_spectrum.propagate_points (pad 3) on the plane spectrum divided by dt x steps so that FP32 seeds stay of order one
physics_configuration.design_variable: dense cell-centred epsilon (float32, one value per cell); the design slab is the pillar layers 24 to 35

rehearsal.supplementary: a 24 um streamed-only member (520 x 520 x 64, 17.3 million cells, 172,800 observers, W=32, K=16, C=4, L=1) with the one-sided difference, docs/validation/g5/G5-05_rehearsal_3060_streamed_24um.json; not judged by this case

reference_method: Directional central finite difference of the same objective along the pillar direction delta (indicator of the pillar cells whose centres lie within 10 um of the axis, over the design slab), two extra streamed forwards in the judged, the optional and the rehearsal runs; in the rehearsal the resident DifferentiablePlaneSimulation on the same grid, sources, monitor and objective is the second reference for the objective and the design-slab gradient.

observables.name: objective
observables.definition: sum over the wavelengths of the on-axis focal intensity

observables.name: focal_intensity_per_frequency
observables.definition: the three terms of the objective

observables.name: plane_electric_energy_per_frequency
observables.definition: |E|^2 integrated over the plane quadrature at each wavelength

observables.name: energy_history
observables.definition: per time step, the sum of squares of the electric Yee samples feeding the plane interpolation (artifact streamed_energy_history.npy)

observables.name: energy_peak_step, energy_rise_step, energy_decayed_fraction
observables.definition: argmax of the history, first step above 1e-3 of the peak, final value over the peak

observables.name: gradient_norm, design_slab_gradient_norm, gradient_nonzero
observables.definition: L2 norms of the dense VJP and of its pillar-layer slab (artifact streamed_design_slab_gradient.npy), count of nonzero entries

observables.name: directional_derivative, finite_difference, relative_error, relative_response
observables.definition: sum of the gradient over the direction cells, (J(eps + h delta) - J(eps)) / h or the central form, |fd - d| / |d|, |delta J| / J

observables.name: frequency_resolution_hz, source_amplitude_ratio
observables.definition: 1 / duration; amplitude spectrum of the sampled source waveform at each wavelength over its peak

propagation.justification: Exploratory streamed forwards of 12 um and 20 um members of the same family reached 1.7e-4 and 2.1e-4 at 160 fs and about 1.5e-4 at 175 fs; the limit leaves a factor of about six for slower lateral leakage of the larger array. A tail of 1e-3 in energy is 3 percent in field amplitude, the truncation error accepted for the spectrum.

spectrum.justification: 1 / 175 fs = 5.71 THz against the 11.72 THz between 1.65 and 1.55 um (0.487); the source amplitude at the three wavelengths is 0.80, 0.99 and 0.75 of its peak.

gradient.justification: The step changes the pillar index by 0.6 percent over 316 pillars (7.7 percent of the 64 um array judged on the RTX 3060, 2.2 percent of the optional 120 um array) and over all 196 pillars in the rehearsal. Both contexts use the central difference: the 14 um rehearsal gave a central relative error of 9.1e-3 at a 26 percent response, while the supplementary 24 um streamed run showed that the one-sided difference at this step carries a 14.7 percent truncation error at a 1.9 percent response (the pillar transmission is strongly nonlinear in epsilon near its resonances), so the one-sided form first declared for the workstation was replaced by the central form before the judged run at the cost of one more forward. The judged and the optional runs keep the 5 percent originally declared for the workstation run and the rehearsal the program's 3 percent physical-parameter threshold. A response below 2e-4 of the objective would sit near the FP32 floor of a 1836-step spectrum and is declared inconclusive (FAIL).

resident_agreement.applies_to: rehearsal only; the judged and optional runs have no resident reference

acceptance_limits.source_of_limits: fixture-specific budgets declared here; resident agreement from proposed_thresholds.discrete_dimensionless_fp32

record.scope: Propagated beyond-VRAM case: a plane-wave pulse through a pillar-array lens, a downsampled spectral output plane, an angular-spectrum focal objective and the dense epsilon VJP. Physical-VRAM comparison, timing and memory figures are stated separately; no throughput superiority or converged design is claimed.

forward_workspace.transfer_scope: Logical workspace payload bytes, not measured PCIe transactions.

forward_memory.accounting_scope: Each field carries its own instrument and overlaps the others; the fields are never added into one total. Torch allocated is a subset of Torch reserved, both are a subset of the device memory of the process; pinned staging appears in the working set and the commit charge; host field banks appear in the working set and in the bank ledger; the OS file cache is system-wide. Caller graphs, optimizer state and the CUDA context are measured only where the process-level instruments include them.
forward_memory.total_memory_note: Not defined: the fields overlap and are never summed.

peak_torch_allocated_bytes.instrument: torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated after the phase (allocator peak counter; the phase set a new process peak, so it is exact)
peak_torch_allocated_bytes.caveat: Torch caching-allocator bytes handed to tensors on this device; a subset of the reserved bytes and of the device memory of the process; excludes the CUDA context, CuPy kernel modules and other processes

peak_torch_reserved_bytes.instrument: torch.cuda.max_memory_reserved after the phase (allocator peak counter; the phase set a new process peak, so it is exact)
peak_torch_reserved_bytes.caveat: Torch caching-allocator bytes held from the driver, including cached blocks not handed to any tensor; contains the allocated bytes, so the two are not added

cuda_process_memory_bytes.instrument: torch.cuda.mem_get_info free-memory decrease during the phase, sampled every 0.02 s and at the end (device-wide, from the driver)
cuda_process_memory_bytes.caveat: Device-wide: includes the Torch reserved bytes (so it is not added to them), the CUDA context, CuPy allocations and any other process on the same device; nvidia-smi per-process used_memory is reported separately when the driver exposes it (it does not under WDDM on Windows)
cuda_process_memory_bytes.nvidia_smi_instrument: nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps reports N/A or is unavailable for this process

peak_process_rss_bytes.instrument: psapi.GetProcessMemoryInfo: WorkingSetSize, PeakWorkingSetSize, PrivateUsage, PagefileUsage, PeakPagefileUsage, working set sampled every 0.02 s and at the phase boundaries
peak_process_rss_bytes.caveat: Host working set (RSS) of the whole process: interpreter, libraries, CUDA runtime host mappings, pinned staging, host field banks and caller tensors; host memory, not device memory; the OS lifetime peak is a process-wide high-water mark that may predate this phase

peak_process_private_bytes.instrument: psapi.GetProcessMemoryInfo: WorkingSetSize, PeakWorkingSetSize, PrivateUsage, PagefileUsage, PeakPagefileUsage, private bytes sampled every 0.02 s and at the phase boundaries
peak_process_private_bytes.caveat: Private (non-shared) host bytes of the process; overlaps the working set and the commit charge

peak_process_committed_bytes.instrument: psapi.GetProcessMemoryInfo: WorkingSetSize, PeakWorkingSetSize, PrivateUsage, PagefileUsage, PeakPagefileUsage, committed bytes sampled every 0.02 s and at the phase boundaries
peak_process_committed_bytes.caveat: Commit charge of the process (Windows PagefileUsage; virtual size on Linux): includes pinned staging and pageable allocations whether resident or not; overlaps the working set

os_file_cache_bytes.instrument: psapi.GetPerformanceInfo: SystemCache pages times PageSize, at the phase boundaries and sampled every 0.02 s
os_file_cache_bytes.caveat: System-wide file cache change during the phase: every process and file on the machine contributes, so it is not attributable to the scratch files alone and can be negative

scratch_disk_written_bytes.instrument: no scratch store in this phase (host banks)
scratch_disk_written_bytes.caveat: Logical bytes written to the scratch bank files; the OS may absorb them in its page cache, so they are not physical storage traffic; the process I/O counters cover every file handle of the process
scratch_disk_written_bytes.process_io_instrument: kernel32.GetProcessIoCounters: ReadTransferCount, WriteTransferCount (all handles, not only scratch files)

scratch_disk_read_bytes.instrument: no scratch store in this phase (host banks)
scratch_disk_read_bytes.caveat: Logical bytes read from the scratch bank files, warm-cache reads included; not physical storage traffic
scratch_disk_read_bytes.process_io_instrument: kernel32.GetProcessIoCounters: ReadTransferCount, WriteTransferCount (all handles, not only scratch files)

scratch_disk_bandwidth_bytes_per_second.instrument: logical scratch bytes divided by the phase wall time, which includes compute and transfers
scratch_disk_bandwidth_bytes_per_second.caveat: an effective rate over the whole phase, not a storage benchmark and not physical bandwidth

scratch_disk_peak_file_bytes.instrument: no scratch store in this phase (host banks)
scratch_disk_peak_file_bytes.caveat: Peak sum of live scratch bank file sizes (files are truncated to the bank size at creation)

host_bank_bytes.instrument: SlabBlockOperator bank ledger: bytes of live host field banks, released through weak references
host_bank_bytes.caveat: Host tensors that also appear in the working set and the commit charge; zero for disk banks, whose sizes are the scratch file bytes
